I could not complete this reliably. The triplet bands give a tentative Dq and B, but I could not fix C.

**Dq.** The ³T₂(F) band is 10Dq, so Dq ≈ 7400/10 = 740 cm⁻¹.

**B.** I took the two ³T₁(F) and ³T₁(P) band positions as the eigenvalues of a 2×2 secular matrix. Their sum is 12660 + 23840 = 36 500 cm⁻¹. Assuming diagonal elements 18Dq (F-based) and 15B + 12Dq (P-based), relative to the ³A₂g ground state, gives 30Dq + 15B = 36 500, so B ≈ 953 cm⁻¹. This depends on my assumed diagonal elements, which I did not verify against a full Tanabe–Sugano matrix.

**Check on the model.** The difference of the two ³T₁ roots (11 180 cm⁻¹) would require an off-diagonal coupling of about 2 635 cm⁻¹, roughly 3.6 Dq. I could not confirm that coefficient from the standard d⁸ matrix. This inconsistency means the B value above is not reliable.

**C.** The ¹E band (15 150 cm⁻¹) fixes C only through the ¹E(D)/¹E(G)/¹A₁(G) singlet block, which I could not reconstruct reliably. A naive diagonal estimate, 18Dq + 10B + 5C, gives a negative C, which signals that the mixing terms are essential. I therefore leave C undetermined.

Dq ≈ 740 cm⁻¹ is the most secure result. B ≈ 950 cm⁻¹ is tentative, and C could not be determined.
